note: Shared glossary for every part of Ovid's Metamorphoses. Entries keyed by word form as printed in Magnus (Gotha: F.A. Perthes), lowercased. Lemma — meaning (grammatical info); the lemma may carry macrons for vowel length, the text never does.

glossary.a: ā — from, by (= ab); a morte: by death
glossary.ab: ab — from, out of; by (agent, + abl.): sorbentur ab ipsa, are swallowed by the earth herself
glossary.aberant: absum — were absent, were far off (3 pl. imperf.)
glossary.abeunt: abeō — go away, turn into (3 pl. pres.; with 'in' + acc., 'change into')
glossary.abiit: abeō — went off into, passed into (3 sg. perf.; in flammas abiit, 'went up in flames')
glossary.ablato: auferō — swept away, carried off (perf. part., m. dat. sg., with 'cervo')
glossary.abscidit: abscīdō — cut off, severed (3 sg. perf.; not abscindō 'tear away')
glossary.abstrahit: abstrahō — drags off, carries away (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.absumitur: absūmō — is used up, wastes away (3 sg. pres. pass. ind.)
glossary.absumptis: absūmō — used up, spent (perf. part., f. abl. pl., abl. absolute with 'viribus')
glossary.ac: ac — and, and also (conj.; = atque, used before consonants)
glossary.accedere: accēdō — to come near, approach (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.accinctus: accingō — girded, equipped (perf. part., m. nom.); quo accinctus erat: with which he was girt
glossary.acclivi: acclīvis — sloping upward, uphill (m. abl. sg., with limite)
glossary.acervo: acervus — heap, mass (m. abl. sg., of separation with 'exemit')
glossary.acres: ācer — fierce, hot, keen (m. nom. pl., with animi 'their tempers')
glossary.acuta: acūtus — sharp, pointed (f. abl. sg., with 'cuspide')
glossary.ad: ad — to, toward; for (+ gerundive of purpose)
glossary.adde: addō — add (2 sg. pres. act. imperat.; here 'add the fact that…', introducing quod)
glossary.addicere: addīcō — to hand over, give up, surrender (pres. act. inf.)
glossary.adductas: addūcō — led along, brought together (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl., with capellas of 676)
glossary.adducto: addūcō — drawn taut, pulled back (perf. part., m. abl. sg., with 'nervo')
glossary.adeo: adeō — so much, to such a degree (adv.; not the verb adeō 'approach')
glossary.aderis: adsum — you will be present, will attend (2 sg. fut.; + dat. 'ducibus')
glossary.adesto: adsum — be present, stand by as witness (2 sg. fut. act. imperat.)
glossary.adeunt: adeō — they approach, go up to (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.adfatur: adfor — addresses, speaks to (3 sg. pres., deponent)
glossary.adfectas: adfectō (affectō) — you reach for, aim at (2 sg. pres. act. ind.; edition's conp-/adf- spelling)
glossary.adfectasse: adfectō — to have aimed at, laid claim to (syncopated perf. inf. = adfectavisse)
glossary.adfert: adferō — brings, supplies (3 sg. pres.; + dat. 'nubibus')
glossary.adfore: adsum — that there would come, be at hand (fut. inf. = adfutūrum esse, in indirect statement)
glossary.adhaesit: adhaereō — came to rest, grounded (3 sg. perf.)
glossary.adiciunt: adiciō — add, throw in (words) (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.adit: adeō — goes to, reaches (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.adiutus: adiuvō — helped, aided (perf. part., m. nom. sg.; + abl. 'pennis')
glossary.admirantibus: admīror — marvelling, wondering at (pres. part. dep., m. dat. pl., 'to those who marvel')
glossary.admisso: admittō — let loose, given full rein (perf. part., m. abl. sg., with 'passu': at full stride)
glossary.admissum: admittō — the offense committed, the crime (perf. part. as noun, n. nom. sg., in indirect question)
glossary.admoverat: admoveō — had brought near, consigned (3 sg. pluperf.; + dat. 'umbris')
glossary.admovit: admoveō — brought near (3 sg. perf.; of a traveller's torch)
glossary.adnuit: adnuō — nodded assent (3 sg. perf.; the present is spelled the same)
glossary.adolentur: adoleō — are burned up (3 pl. pres. pass.)
glossary.adopertaque: adoperiō — and having covered (perf. part., f. nom. + -que)
glossary.adorant: adōrō — they worship, pray to (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.adsensibus: adsēnsus — shouts of assent, approval (m. abl. pl.)
glossary.adsere: adserō — lay claim to (2 sg. imper.; with 'nec' = a prohibition, 'do not claim')
glossary.adsidua: adsiduus (assiduus) — unceasing, unremitting (f. abl. sg., with vertigine)
glossary.adsiduis: adsiduus — unceasing, constant (f. abl. pl., with 'nubibus')
glossary.adspergine: aspergō — by the sprinkling, spray (abl.; older spelling adsp-)
glossary.adspice: adspiciō (aspiciō) — look at, behold (2 sg. pres. act. imperat.)
glossary.adspicit: adspiciō (aspiciō) — looks upon, beholds (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.adspirate: adspīrō — breathe upon, favor (2 pl. imperative; + dat. 'coeptis')
glossary.adstricta: adstringō — bound tight, frozen fast (perf. part., f. nom. sg., with 'glacies')
glossary.adunca: aduncus — curved, hooked (f. abl. sg., with 'cumba')
glossary.adversas: adversus — facing, in their path (f. acc. pl., with 'vestes')
glossary.adversi: adversus — facing, turned to meet you (m. gen. sg., with tauri)
glossary.adversum: adversus — the opposing direction (n. acc. sg. as noun: in adversum 'against the current, uphill')
glossary.aeas: Aeās — the Aeas, a river of Epirus/Thessaly and its river-god (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.aegaeona: Aegaeōn — Aegaeon (Briareus), the hundred-armed sea-giant (m. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.aemula: aemulus — rival of, emulating (f. nom. sg.; + gen. 'Phoebes')
glossary.aenea: aēneus — of bronze, bronze (f. nom. sg., with 'proles')
glossary.aeoliis: Aeolius — Aeolian, of Aeolus the wind-king (n. abl. pl., with 'antris')
glossary.aequalibus: aequālis — equal, even (n. abl. pl., with spatiis 'at equal intervals')
glossary.aequalis: aequālis — even, uniform (f. nom. sg., predicative with 'terram'); at I.750 instead the adjective used as a noun, m. nom. sg. of Phaethon — a match, an equal ('animis aequalis et annis', matched in spirit and in years)
glossary.aequi: aequum — what is right, justice (n. gen. sg., after 'amantior'; not aequus 'level')
glossary.aequo: aequus — level, equal (n. abl.); ex aequo: on equal terms
glossary.aequor: aequor — the sea, the level expanse (n. nom. sg.)
glossary.aequora: aequor — the open sea, the sea-plains (n. acc. pl., after 'in')
glossary.aequoris: aequor — of the sea (gen.); aequoris instar: like the sea
glossary.aer: āēr — air, the air (m. nom. sg., Greek noun)
glossary.aere: aēr — air (m. abl. sg.) at 12, 23; at 92 and 115 aes 'bronze' (n. abl. sg.)
glossary.aesculeae: aesculeus — of oak, oaken (f. gen. sg., with 'frondis')
glossary.aestas: aestās — Summer, here personified as one of the seasons (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.aestu: aestus — heat (m. abl. sg., of cause)
glossary.aestusque: aestus — spells of heat, summers (m. acc. pl.) + -que
glossary.aeternum: aeternus — everlasting (n. nom. sg., with 'ver'); at I.663 instead n. acc. sg. agreeing with 'aevum' in 'in aevum' — into an everlasting age
glossary.aether: aethēr — upper air, sky (m. nom. sg., Greek noun)
glossary.aethera: aethēr — upper air, sky (m. acc. sg., Greek acc.)
glossary.aethere: aethēr — upper air, sky (m. abl. sg., of source)
glossary.aetheriis: aetherius — of the upper air, of the sky (m. abl. pl., with 'solibus')
glossary.aetherioque: aetherius — heavenly, of the sky (n. abl. sg., with 'sidere'; + -que 'and')
glossary.aethiopasque: Aethiopes — the Ethiopians (m. acc. pl., Greek acc.; + -que 'and')
glossary.aevum: aevum — age, era (n. acc. sg., with 'in')
glossary.agat: agō — would drive (3 sg. pres. act. subj., potential)
glossary.agere: agō — to keep, maintain (silence) (pres. inf., in indirect statement after 'vidit')
glossary.ages: agō — will you do (2 sg. fut. act. ind.)
glossary.agit: agō — drives, herds (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.agitabilis: agitābilis — easily stirred, mobile (m. nom. sg., with 'aer')
glossary.agitantia: agitō — stirring up, driving (pres. act. part., n. acc. pl., with nubila)
glossary.agitasse: agitō — to have shaken, tossed (syncopated perf. inf. = agitāvisse)
glossary.agitataque: agitō — shaken, tossed about (perf. part., n. acc. pl., with 'robora'; + -que)
glossary.ait: aiō — says, said (3 sg.; defective verb)
glossary.alas: āla — wings (f. acc. pl.; Mercury's winged sandals)
glossary.aliis: alius — to the others, other things (n. dat. pl., with 'obstabat')
glossary.alipedum: ālipēs — wing-footed, swift as wings (adj., m. gen. pl., with equorum)
glossary.aliquam: aliquī — some, some sort of (f. acc. sg., with 'faciem')
glossary.aliter: aliter — otherwise; non aliter quam: just as
glossary.aliud: alius — another thing, one thing (n. nom. sg.; 'aliud … aliis' = one another)
glossary.alta: altus — deep (n. acc. pl. at 349, with 'silentia'; f. nom. sg. earlier, with 'nix'); at I.630 f. abl. sg. with 'tellure' ('sub alta tellure', beneath the deep earth); at II.1 f. nom. sg. with 'regia' in the sense high, lofty; at II.71 n. acc. pl. with 'sidera', the high stars
glossary.altae: altus — lofty, deep (f. gen. sg., with 'mentis')
glossary.altior: altus — higher (compar., f. nom. sg., with 'unda')
glossary.altissima: altus — highest (superl., f. nom. sg., with via understood: the road is highest at mid-heaven)
glossary.altissimus: altus — highest (superl., m. nom. sg., with sol)
glossary.alto: altus — high (n. abl. with 'aethere': ab alto aethere, from the high aether); also 'deep'
glossary.altoque: altus — deep, intense (m. abl. sg., with 'aestu'; + -que)
glossary.altorum: altus — tall, deep (n. gen. pl., with nemorum)
glossary.altos: altus — high, lofty (m. acc. pl., with currus)
glossary.amantior: amāns — more loving of, fonder of (compar., m. nom. sg.; + gen. 'aequi')
glossary.amantis: amāns — a lover (pres. part. as noun, m. gen. sg., with 'nomen')
glossary.amara: amārus — bitter (f. abl. sg., with herba)
glossary.amatum: amō — beloved (perf. part., n. acc.); corpus amatum: the beloved body
glossary.ambiguo: ambiguum — doubt, uncertainty (n. abl. sg.; in ambiguo est, 'is in doubt')
glossary.ambiguum: at I.765 ambiguus — uncertain, undecided (n. nom. sg., used impersonally: '[it is] unclear whether … or'); at II.9 instead of Proteus, shifting, of changeable shape (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.ambitae: ambiō — encircled, surrounded (perf. part., f. gen. sg., with 'terrae')
glossary.amissam: āmittō — lost (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg., 'as one lost')
glossary.amnes: amnis — rivers (m. acc. pl.); at I.581 instead m. nom. pl., subject of 'deducunt' ('amnes alii', the other rivers)
glossary.amnis: amnis — of the river (m. gen. sg. with magni — not the nominative; 'the inner chambers of the great river')
glossary.amor: amor — love (m. nom. sg.); at 480 and 532 Amor, the god Love (Cupid)
glossary.amore: amor — love (m. abl. sg., abl. of agent/means with victus)
glossary.amores: amor — loves, love-affairs (m. acc. pl., poetic pl.); at 461 object of 'inritare'; earlier 'her beloved'
glossary.amoris: Amor — Love, the god Cupid (m. gen. sg.; capitalised in the edition)
glossary.amphitrite: Amphitrītē — Amphitrite, sea-goddess, wife of Neptune; here the sea itself (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.amphrysos: Amphrȳsos — the Amphrysus, a Thessalian river and its river-god (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.amplexaque: amplector — and having embraced (deponent perf. part., f. nom. + -que)
glossary.an: an — whether (in indirect question, 223); at 196 introducing a direct question, 'do you really…?'; at I.586 whether ('an sit apud manes'); at I.765 the second member of a double indirect question, 'or' ('precibus … an ira', by prayers or rather by anger)
glossary.anguipedum: anguipēs — of the snake-footed ones, i.e. the Giants (m. gen. pl.)
glossary.animalia: animal — living creatures (n.; acc. pl. at 416, 425; nom. pl. at 464)
glossary.animalibus: animal — living creatures (n. abl. pl., with 'orba')
glossary.animas: anima — souls, breath of life (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.animasse: animō — to have given life to, quickened (syncopated perf. inf. = animavisse)
glossary.animi: animus — spirits, tempers (m. nom. pl.; of the horses)
glossary.animis: animus — at I.750 in spirit (m. abl. pl., abl. of respect with aequalis); at II.39 instead from our mind (m. dat. pl., dat. of separation with detrahe)
glossary.animo: animus — mind, heart (m. abl. sg., of place where)
glossary.animoque: animus — and with the mind, heart (abl. + -que)
glossary.animosos: animōsus — spirited, mettlesome (m. acc. pl., with quadrupedes)
glossary.anni: annus — year (m. gen. sg., with 'longi'; not nom. pl.)
glossary.annis: annus — at I.750 in years (m. abl. pl., abl. of respect); at II.55 instead to years (m. dat. pl., with conveniant)
glossary.annum: annus — the year (m. acc. sg., object of 'exegit')
glossary.annus: annus — the Year, here personified beside Day and Month (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.ante: ante — before, earlier (adverb, at 442 and 487); before, in front of (prep. + acc., at 563)
glossary.antiquas: antīquus — ancient, of old (f. acc. pl., with 'figuras')
glossary.antiqui: antīquus — old, former (n. gen. sg., with 'veris')
glossary.antiquo: antīquus — old, former (m. abl. sg., with 'alveo')
glossary.antra: antrum — caves (n. nom. pl., predicate of 'fuerunt')
glossary.anxia: anxius — anxious, uneasy (f. nom. sg.; + gen. furti 'about the intrigue')
glossary.aonios: Aonius — Aonian, Boeotian (m. acc. pl.; a noun like 'agros' understood)
glossary.apertis: aperiō — thrown open (perf. part., f. abl. pl., with 'valvis')
glossary.aperto: aperiō — open, plain (perf. part., n. abl. sg., with 'discrimine')
glossary.apertos: apertus — open, unobstructed (m. acc. pl., with 'campos')
glossary.apidanusque: Apidanus — the Apidanus, a Thessalian river and its river-god (m. nom. sg.; + -que 'and')
glossary.apollineas: Apollineus — Apollo's, of Apollo (f. acc. pl., with 'medullas')
glossary.apta: aptus — suited, fitted (f. nom. sg., with 'concordia'; + dat. 'fetibus')
glossary.aptamque: aptus — suited, fit (f. acc. sg., with umbram; + dat. pastoribus; + -que 'and')
glossary.aptato: aptō — fitted, set in place (perf. part., m. abl.); aptato mucrone: the point set
glossary.aptos: aptus — fit, suited (m. acc. pl.) + dat.
glossary.apud: apud — among, in the presence of (prep. + acc.)
glossary.aquae: aqua — water (f. gen. sg.); at 432 with 'pugnax', at odds with water (gen., or dat.)
glossary.aquarum: aqua — of the waters (f. gen. pl.)
glossary.aquilone: Aquilō — the North Wind (m. abl. sg., of means with 'remotis')
glossary.aquilonem: Aquilō — the North Wind (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.aquis: aqua — water (f. abl. pl.); here abl. of means: mollit aquis, he softens with water
glossary.arae: āra — altars (f. nom. pl.; not gen./dat. sg.)
glossary.ararat: arō — had ploughed (3 sg. pluperf., syncopated = arāverat)
glossary.arbore: arbor — tree (f. abl. sg.); at 451 with 'de', from any tree at all; earlier abl. of source, 'patula Iovis arbore'
glossary.arborei: arboreus — of the tree (m. nom. pl.); arborei fetus: the tree's fruit
glossary.arboreis: arboreus — of trees, tree- (f. abl. pl., with frondibus)
glossary.arboribus: arbor — trees (f. abl. pl., abl. of means with consita)
glossary.arbuteos: arbuteus — of the arbutus, strawberry-tree (m. acc. pl., with 'fetus')
glossary.arcadiae: Arcadia — Arcadia, the mountainous inland region of the Peloponnese (f. gen. sg.)
glossary.arcadis: Arcas — the Arcadian, i.e. Lycaon (m. gen. sg., with 'tyranni')
glossary.arcus: arcus — bow (m. nom. sg.); at II.81 m. acc. pl. (4th decl. -ūs), governed by 'per' — the Haemonian bows, i.e. the Archer
glossary.ardeat: ardeō — should blaze, catch fire (3 sg. pres. subj.)
glossary.ardent: ardeō — blaze up, catch fire (3 pl. pres.)
glossary.ardentibus: ārdeō — burning, eager (pres. part., n. abl. pl., with 'studiis')
glossary.ardentior: ārdēns — hotter, more burning (comparative, f. nom. sg., of the fifth zone)
glossary.ardesceret: ardēscō — would catch fire, blaze up (3 sg. imperf. subj., after 'ne')
glossary.arduus: arduus — steep, lofty (m. nom. sg., with 'aether')
glossary.arestoridae: Arestoridēs — son of Arestor, patronymic of Argus (m. dat. sg.)
glossary.arge: Argus — Argus, the hundred-eyed herdsman (m. voc. sg.)
glossary.argentea: argenteus — of silver (f. nom. sg., with 'proles')
glossary.argenteus: argenteus — of silver, silver (m. nom. sg., with ordo)
glossary.argo: Argus — Argus, the hundred-eyed herdsman set to guard Io (m. dat. sg. in all three lines)
glossary.argolicae: Argolicus — Argive, of Argos (f. gen. sg., with paelicis; of Io)
glossary.argum: Argus — Argus, the hundred-eyed herdsman (m. acc. sg.)
glossary.argus: Argus — Argus, the hundred-eyed herdsman (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.aristis: arista — ears of grain (f. abl. pl.); at 492 abl. absolute 'demptis aristis', the ears once stripped off; earlier of means
glossary.arma: arma — arms, weapons (n. acc. pl.; plural only)
glossary.armenta: armentum — herds of cattle (n. acc. pl.)
glossary.armento: armentum — herd (n. abl. sg.; quo armento 'from what herd')
glossary.arquitenens: arquitenēns — the Bow-bearer, the Archer (m. nom. sg., of Apollo; the edition's spelling for arcitenens)
glossary.arte: ars — skill, means (f. abl. sg., with 'qua')
glossary.artibus: ars — arts, crafts (f. abl. pl., with 'paternis')
glossary.artior: artus — narrower, tighter (compar. adj., m. nom. sg., with orbis)
glossary.artus: artus — limbs (m. acc. pl., object of 'mollit')
glossary.arvis: arvum — fields, ploughland (n. abl. pl., after 'ab')
glossary.aspera: asper — rough, harsh (n. nom. pl., with 'loca')
glossary.astra: astrum — stars (n.; acc. pl. at 316, object of 'petit'; nom. pl. earlier)
glossary.astraea: Astraea — Astraea, goddess of Justice, last of the gods to leave earth (f. nom. sg.)
glossary.atlantiades: Atlantiadēs — the descendant of Atlas, i.e. Mercury, grandson of Atlas through Maia (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.atram: āter — black, dark (f. acc.); in atram faciem: to a dark hue
glossary.attonitum: attonō — thunderstruck, stunned (perf. part., m. acc. sg., with 'ausum')
glossary.auctaque: augeō — increased, enhanced (perf. part., f. nom. sg., with 'forma'; + -que)
glossary.auctor: auctor — originator, source; at II.88 the giver (of a gift) (m. nom. sg. in both lines)
glossary.audita: audiō — heard (perf. part., f. nom. sg., with 'bucina')
glossary.auditque: audiō — hears (3 sg. pres. act. ind.; + -que 'and')
glossary.auferat: auferō — may carry off, sweep away (3 sg. pres. act. subj., in a ne clause of fearing/purpose)
glossary.auget: augeō — increases, swells (3 sg. pres. act. ind.)
glossary.auguste: Augustus — Augustus, the emperor (m. voc. sg.)
glossary.augustis: Augustus — of Augustus, the emperor's (m. abl. pl., with 'postibus'; could also be the adjective augustus 'revered', but the edition capitalises)
glossary.aura: aura — breeze (f.); nom. sg. at 529, subject of 'dabat'; abl. of comparison at 502, 'ocior aura levi', swifter than a light breeze
glossary.auratum: aurātus — golden, gilded (n. nom. sg., of the arrow)
glossary.aureus: aureus — golden, of gold (m. nom. sg.; twice in II.107, of axis and temo)
glossary.auris: aura — breezes (f. abl. pl., with 'tepentibus'); not auris 'ear'
glossary.auro: aurum — than gold (n. abl. sg., of comparison with 'deterior'); at II.2 instead a plain abl. of means with 'micante', gleaming with gold
glossary.auroram: Aurōra — Aurora, the Dawn; here the East (f. acc. sg.)
glossary.austro: Auster — the South Wind (m. abl. sg., with 'ab')
glossary.ausum: audeō — the one who had dared (perf. part. as noun, m. acc. sg.)
glossary.autumnus: autumnus — Autumn, here personified as one of the seasons (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.auxiliaribus: auxiliāris — helping, reinforcing (f. abl. pl., with 'undis')
glossary.aversata: āversor — having spurned, turned away from (perf. part. of a deponent, f. nom. sg.; active in sense, + acc. 'petentes')
glossary.aversus: āvertō — turned away (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.: 'though turned away')
glossary.avia: avius — pathless, trackless (n. acc. pl., with 'nemora'); at I.701 the adjective used as a noun, n. acc. pl. after 'per' — through trackless country
glossary.avidissima: avidus — most greedy for (superlative, f. nom. sg., + gen. 'caedis')
glossary.axe: axis — axle; by extension the chariot (m. abl. sg.)
glossary.axis: axis — the axle of the sky, the heavens (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.barba: barba — beard (f.; nom. sg. at 266, abl. sg. at 339 with 'madida')
glossary.beatum: beātus — blessed, made happy (m. acc. sg., with nescio quem)
glossary.bifores: biforis — two-leaved, double, folding (f. nom. pl., with valvae)
glossary.bina: bīnī — two at a time, two apiece (distributive numeral, n. nom. pl., with lumina understood from 625)
glossary.blandis: blandus — coaxing, caressing (m. abl. pl., with 'lacertis')
glossary.blanditias: blanditia — coaxing words, endearments (f. acc. pl.)
glossary.bonis: bonum — goods, good things (n. abl. pl., after e(que) 'from')
glossary.boreas: Boreās — Boreas, the North Wind (m. nom. sg.)
glossary.bove: bōs — cow, heifer (f. abl. sg., after de)
glossary.bracchia: bracchium — arms (n.; nom. pl. at 550, subject of 'crescunt'; acc. pl. earlier)
